lab_title: Anatomy of the Human Heart and the Pathway of Blood Flow
top_level_objectives: Identify the four chambers, four valves, and major blood vessels of the human heart in 3D space.
Trace the chronological pathway of blood flow through both the pulmonary and systemic circulation loops.
Explain the functional significance of the structural differences in myocardial thickness between the left and right ventricles.
Describe how the heart valves operate mechanically to ensure unidirectional blood flow during the cardiac cycle.

scenes.brief_purpose: Introduce the anatomical orientation of the heart and identify the external great vessels entering and leaving it.
key_visuals: A high-fidelity 3D human heart positioned within a semi-transparent thoracic cavity of an adult torso.
Color-coded great vessels: blue for the superior and inferior vena cava and pulmonary trunk; red for the aorta and pulmonary veins.
Interactive anatomical direction indicators (Anterior, Posterior, Superior, Inferior).
student_actions: Rotate and scale the 3D heart to examine its anterior and posterior surfaces.
Tap and label the Superior Vena Cava, Inferior Vena Cava, Aorta, Pulmonary Trunk, and Pulmonary Veins.
Answer a placement question identifying which vessels carry blood toward the heart versus away from it.

scenes.brief_purpose: Explore the four internal chambers of the heart and investigate the structural differences in myocardial thickness.
key_visuals: A coronal cross-section of the 3D heart revealing the right atrium, right ventricle, left atrium, and left ventricle.
Highlight overlays on the muscular walls (myocardium) of both the left and right ventricles, emphasizing the difference in wall thickness.
A virtual caliper tool for measuring tissue thickness.
student_actions: Identify and select each of the four chambers based on anatomical descriptions.
Use the virtual caliper to measure and compare the thickness of the right ventricular wall versus the left ventricular wall.
Solve a multiple-choice question explaining why the left ventricle requires a significantly thicker myocardium than the right ventricle (pumping to systemic vs. pulmonary circulation).

scenes.brief_purpose: Examine the anatomy and physical mechanics of the four heart valves in preventing backflow.
key_visuals: Close-up interior views of the Atrioventricular (AV) valves (tricuspid and mitral/bicuspid) showing chordae tendineae and papillary muscles.
Close-up interior views of the Semilunar valves (pulmonary and aortic).
An interactive animation showing the open and closed states of the valves during atrial and ventricular contraction.
student_actions: Tap to label the tricuspid, mitral, pulmonary, and aortic valves.
Manually manipulate a temporal slider to watch the valves open and close in slow motion during a cardiac cycle.
Interact with a 'pressure simulation' where dragging blood backwards demonstrates how valve cusps catch fluid to prevent regurgitation.

scenes.brief_purpose: Trace the pathway of deoxygenated blood through the right side of the heart to the lungs (Pulmonary Circuit).
key_visuals: Blue glowing particles representing deoxygenated blood entering the heart.
A visual pathway highlighting the right atrium, tricuspid valve, right ventricle, pulmonary valve, pulmonary trunk, and pulmonary arteries.
A simplified schematic of the lungs on either side of the heart model.
student_actions: Initiate the blood flow animation and follow the blue particles as they enter from the vena cavae.
Sequentially tap the anatomical structures in the exact order that a red blood cell would experience them from systemic return to pulmonary exit.
Confirm understanding of gas exchange by identifying that blood in the pulmonary arteries is deoxygenated despite being in an artery.

scenes.brief_purpose: Trace the pathway of oxygenated blood returning from the lungs through the left side of the heart to the body (Systemic Circuit).
key_visuals: Red glowing particles representing oxygenated blood returning from the pulmonary veins.
A visual pathway highlighting the left atrium, mitral/bicuspid valve, left ventricle, aortic valve, and aorta.
An interactive schematic of the systemic capillary beds representing the body tissues.
student_actions: Trigger the flow of oxygenated blood from the pulmonary veins into the left atrium.
Sequentially tap the left-side structures in the correct physiological order to complete the systemic ejection sequence.
Compare the velocity and pressure visualization of blood leaving the aorta versus blood leaving the pulmonary trunk.

scenes.scene_name: The Complete Cardiac Cycle and Synthesis
scenes.brief_purpose: Synthesize the complete, continuous dual-loop cardiac cycle and assess overall comprehension of heart anatomy.
key_visuals: A fully animated, beating 3D heart demonstrating synchronized dual-loop circulation (simultaneous blue and red blood flows).
An interactive drag-and-drop flow chart interface mapped directly over the 3D heart model.
A diagnostic scenario card representing a clinical case study (e.g., mitral valve regurgitation).
student_actions: Drag and drop the names of chambers, valves, and vessels into a chronological 12-step pathway puzzle representing a single red blood cell's journey.
Observe the synchronized beating heart and identify which valves are open/closed during systole vs. diastole.
Analyze the clinical scenario card to predict how a leaky mitral valve would affect oxygenation and pressure in the left atrium and lungs.
